metaData.originalTitle: How Harmonic Rebuilt Scout on Deep Agents and 4x'd Retention with LangSmith
metaData.title: How Harmonic Rebuilt Scout on Deep Agents and 4x'd Retention with LangSmith
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Harmonic rebuilt its Scout AI agent on LangChain's Deep Agents and LangSmith, simplifying architecture, enabling emergent use cases, and achieving 4x week-1-to-week-4 retention and 10x average session duration.
metaData.summary: This article details how Harmonic, a startup intelligence platform for venture capital, rebuilt its Scout AI agent. The first version used a rigid, multi-subgraph pipeline that required constant tuning and failed on open-ended user requests. The V2 architecture is a deliberate simplification: a single frontier model in a Deep Agents harness with access to two tool categories—one for Harmonic's global data layer (40M companies, 200M people) and one for firm-specific context (CRM, emails, connections). This shift unlocked emergent use cases like personalized outreach drafts and abstract investment thesis searches. The article highlights key UX design principles, such as ensuring the model can see everything the user sees (shared filesystem for search results, inline rendering of visualizations). LangSmith Deployment handles durable execution, scaling, and observability, while LangSmith Engine identifies failure modes and suggests improvements. The results are dramatic: 4x retention and 10x session duration, allowing Harmonic to expand its TAM beyond VC firms to innovation, corporate development, and GTM teams.

mainPoints.point: Simplifying agent architecture from a rigid multi-graph pipeline to a single frontier model with tools dramatically improved capability and iteration speed.
mainPoints.explanation: Scout V1's complex subgraph system required hundreds of evals and failed on novel intents. V2's Deep Agents harness, with a smart model and well-designed tools, handled open-ended tasks out of the box, reducing iteration from months to days.

mainPoints.point: A key UX principle for agents is that the model must be able to discover everything the user sees.
mainPoints.explanation: To handle follow-up questions, Scout V2 uses a shared filesystem for search results and renders visualizations inline. This ensures the model has context on the artifacts it generates, preventing conversational dead ends.

mainPoints.point: The new architecture enabled emergent use cases, transforming Scout from a search tool into a trusted investment advisor.
mainPoints.explanation: Users now hand Scout an investment thesis for company recommendations or ask for pre-meeting briefs that synthesize CRM, emails, and public data. This shift unlocked a 10x increase in average session duration.

mainPoints.point: LangSmith's platform layer (Deployment, Engine) allowed a lean team to focus on product differentiation rather than infrastructure.
mainPoints.explanation: LangSmith Deployment provided 'set and forget' durable execution and scaling. LangSmith Engine automated failure mode analysis and suggested code improvements, creating a self-improving loop.

keyQuotes: The model has the agency it needs to not run into dead ends. We're always checking ourselves to keep the graph as simple as possible.
Agents love things that feel like code. Users hate things that feel like code.
Not having to build a unique workflow experience for every individual use case or customers is a huge unlock.

Before Scout, we'd build for how we expected users to interact with our product... Now, in this agentic model, we give users the ability to interact with the data how they want to and we observe how they use it.
